name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia-retinitis pigmentosa syndrome
aliases: Primary ciliary dyskinesia with retinitis pigmentosa

criteria.description: Clinical and electrophysiological evidence of retinitis pigmentosa
Electron microscopy showing ciliary ultrastructural abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with PCD-RP syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic sinopulmonary infections, retinitis pigmentosa, and ciliary ultrastructural defects or pathogenic genetic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pulmonology, ophthalmology, and genetic testing.

searchTerms: long-term cough with mucus and lung damage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Retinitis pigmentosa with progressive peripheral vision loss
searchTerms: night blindness with narrowing side vision
progressive peripheral vision loss from retinal degeneration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal ciliary ultrastructure on electron microscopy
searchTerms: abnormal tiny hair-like structures on cells
long-lasting sinus infection with nasal blockage
chronic sinus inflammation causing stuffy nose

common.symptomName: Situs inversus or other laterality defects
searchTerms: organs reversed or misplaced in body
low nitric oxide in nasal airways

occasional.symptomName: Mild hearing loss due to chronic otitis media
searchTerms: mild hearing loss from ear infections
slight deafness due to chronic middle ear problems
hearing reduction linked to otitis media

rare.symptomName: Infertility due to impaired sperm motility or ciliary dysfunction in fallopian tubes
searchTerms: infertility from poor sperm or egg tube movement
reproductive issues due to cilia dysfunction
difficulty conceiving from sperm or fallopian tube problems

laboratory: Sputum cultures positive for chronic bacterial colonization
other: Abnormal ciliary beat pattern on high-speed video microscopy
Electroretinography showing rod-cone dystrophy consistent with retinitis pigmentosa

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of situs inversus with PCD but absence of retinitis pigmentosa
Retinal degeneration without respiratory or ciliary dysfunction
Pancreatic insufficiency and elevated sweat chloride test
Different genetic mutations and absence of retinitis pigmentosa

redFlags: Progressive peripheral vision loss with night blindness
Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections with bronchiectasis
Abnormal ciliary ultrastructure on electron microscopy
references: Lucas JS, et al. Primary ciliary dyskinesia: diagnosis and management. Eur Respir J. 2017.
Zhao C, et al. Genetic and clinical features of primary ciliary dyskinesia with retinitis pigmentosa. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2021.
Knowles MR, et al. Primary ciliary dyskinesia. Clin Chest Med. 2016.
